correctness.rationale: For each k>=1, explicit derivative and |f_prime|<=4k give 1/2<=density<=3/2 and uniform margins, and ∂u F(v|u)=-2 eps f<0 proves SI. The xi integral is exactly 2 eps^2 I_k, with beta I_k=4^(2k)(2k)!^2/(4k+1)!. The four quadrant masses yield ξ(checkerboard)=eps^2/2 via independently integrated conditional CDF, so ratio=1/(4I_k); Gaussian dominated convergence gives I_k~sqrt(pi/(8k)). Direct exact fractions show the first k with I_k<1/4 is 6. Standalone checker reproduces 16 finite cases. Analytic proof, not enumeration, establishes the infinite result.

originality.rationale: The v2 lead preprint already gives a fixed twofold SI checkerboard overestimate; that statement is explicitly prior, not new. It proves a lower bound only for density-TP2 input. In contrast, this theorem rules out any finite multiplicative checkerboard bound even with smooth strictly positive SI density uniformly between 1/2 and 3/2 and a fixed 2x2 grid. The full source and its appendix supply neither the growing ratio nor an implication establishing it, while the continuity literature concerns other quantifiers. Targeted published-finding corpus searches found no dominating published result; absence is not a priority certificate.
residual_risks: The source establishes a twofold SI counterexample already; novelty is restricted to the growing multiplier in the smooth uniformly density-bounded SI family.
Other equivalently parameterized families with arbitrarily large checkerboard inflation could exist outside the indexed records; originality search cannot certify unique priority.
The theorem proves relative inflation only, with both statistics vanishing; it does not imply a universal positive absolute error.
No claim against the established density-TP2 lower inequality or against fixed-copula fine-grid consistency.

value.rationale: The precise scientific gap is quantitative stability after relaxing a published TP2 density condition to SI. A known SI counterexample with fixed inflation 2 does not determine whether a weaker multiplicative guarantee survives. Proving every finite multiplicative bound fails, even for strictly positive polynomial densities with a uniform 1/2-to-3/2 bound and fixed 2x2 resolution, supplies a structural obstruction important to the interpretation of checkerboard directed-dependence diagnostics. The entire natural k>=1 family has an exact ratio and asymptotics. This is not a tiny numerical refinement, trivial renaming or table entry.
